task: You support the VP of Engineering at a code-hosting platform, and leadership wants to know how healthy the delivery process is. Find out how quickly work gets merged, whether it is reviewed and how reliable production deployments are.

produce.name: Pull request outcomes
produce.about: Pull requests and share in each state.

produce.name: Time to merge
produce.about: Merged pull requests and average hours to merge for each language.

produce.name: Review coverage
produce.about: Merged pull requests with no review and with no approval.

produce.name: Change failure
produce.about: Production deploys, failures and the change failure rate per month.

summaries.understand-data: List a merged pull request's reviews and look for one merged with none.
summaries.pr-outcomes: Count pull requests that were merged, closed or are still open.
summaries.cycle-time: Compare average time to merge across languages.
summaries.review-coverage: Count merged pull requests with no review or no approval.
summaries.change-failure: Track the share of production deploys that fail each month.
summaries.synthesis: Choose the one process change that would most improve delivery.
summaries.report: Write three findings and one recommendation.

problems: Merged pull requests also have a closed time, so only the merge time tells merged work from abandoned work.
185 pull requests are still open and have no outcome yet.
1,184 merged pull requests have no review at all.
Many pull requests have several reviews, up to six, so joining reviews repeats each pull request.
Deployments mix staging and production, and a failure is either failed or rolled back.
Time to merge is skewed: the average is about 22 hours, the median about 15, and the longest about four weeks.
